passages.note: House final-passage Yea in 2023 (same legislature, earlier chamber); 6 Nays of 75 members is under 10%, so it cannot carry a chair alone.

passages.provision_quote: without written parental consent make changes to a student's education record
passages.note: Operative text guarantees parental access to the education record and requires parental consent for gender-identity changes to the record, not for staff use of a name or pronouns, and it neither requires nor rules out school notification; it shows only the parental-rights side.

rows.reasoning: Stratton voted Yea on SB 100 (2023), which bars schools from shielding a student's education record from parents and requires written parental consent before changing the record's gender identity. That places him on the parental-rights side, but the bill's object is the education record, not staff use of 'a different name or pronouns' (rung 5), and it does not say schools must 'notify parents' (rung 4) or only tell them 'when parents ask' (rung 3); the vote is also near-unanimous.
